secondaryWeapon: Deimos Sage Shield, later converted to Astra Arcane Shield
archetype: Teleport-based Explorer mage with a strong 2-minute burst, a good full-rotation DPM profile for solo bossing, and the longest bind in the game. Damage is gated on a freeze-stack resource: ice skills apply stacks, lightning skills consume them, and several passives pay out only while stacks are up. Easy mobbing, simple burst, cheap to bring online, which also makes it a commonly recommended boss mule and champion mule.

linkSkill.name: Empirical Knowledge
linkSkill.effect: Passive. Attacks have a 31% chance at master level to identify the weakness of the struck enemy with the highest Max HP, granting +5% damage and +5% enemy DEF ignored per stack for 10 seconds. Stacks up to 3 times, one stack per unique Explorer Magician job character on the world.

priority.node: Build the four boost node groups that correspond to the 6th job mastery cores first: (1) Chain Lightning, (2) Frozen Orb + Blizzard, (3) Lightning Orb, (4) Thunder Sphere + Elquines.
priority.why: These are four of the six boost node groups, and they are the four the sources single out. The class doc states verbatim: 'Ice/Lightning has four relevant boost nodes that must be upgraded first' (the accompanying list is an image and was not transcribed; the four group identities come from the other two sources). Grandis Library's page data marks node groups 1-4 as PRIMARY and defines PRIMARY as 'Boost Nodes that unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery and are skills that are frequently used'. NamuWiki heads an 'Essential Reinforcing Core' table with the matching 6th job core names (Chain Lightning VI, Frozen Orb VI / Blizzard VI, Lightning Spear VI, Thunder Spear VI / Elquines VI) and says it 'strengthens 4 cores out of a total of 6 reinforcement cores'. The class doc separately confirms the pairing skill-by-skill, describing Chain Lightning, Frozen Orb, Blizzard, Elquines and Lightning Orb each as 'Boosted by V Boost nodes' and 'given a VI Job Mastery Core'.
priority.consensusNote: Three independent sources agree on which four groups matter and on the group contents (class doc, Grandis Library, NamuWiki KMS). The four-groups statement itself is in the class doc's own prose; the contents are confirmed by Grandis's structured page data and by NamuWiki independently.
priority.correctionNote: An earlier version of this entry added 'so boost node investment is also the gate on 6th job progress'. That causal gating mechanic is asserted by no source and has been removed. The class doc presents boost nodes and mastery cores as separate upgrade tracks. Grandis's PRIMARY legend does use the word 'unlock' about the relationship, so that wording is now quoted and attributed rather than generalised into a progression gate.

priority.node: Leave the remaining two boost node groups for last, and treat them as two different tiers rather than one: Frost Ward + Ice Strike is the lesser-but-still-used group; Thunder Bolt + Cold Beam is the one you can skip.
priority.why: Grandis Library's page data puts Frost Ward + Ice Strike in SECONDARY, defined as 'Boost Nodes that don't unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery but are still used', and puts Thunder Bolt + Cold Beam alone in OTHER, defined as 'Boost Nodes that do not need to be upgraded or has least priority'. NamuWiki matches the split: it lists Glacial Wall (Frost Ward) / Ice Strike as the 'select strengthening core' and does not list Cold Beam / Thunderbolt among either the essential or selectable cores. NamuWiki also gives the narrow exception verbatim: 'Ice Strike is used in some hunting builds before the opening of Frozen of VI', i.e. before HEXA Frozen Orb is unlocked.
priority.consensusNote: Two independent sources (Grandis, NamuWiki) agree on both the split and the ordering. The Ice Strike training exception is single-source and KMS-side.
priority.correctionNote: An earlier version said 'Grandis Library ranks both in its lowest tier'. It does not: Grandis ranks Frost Ward + Ice Strike SECONDARY and only Thunder Bolt + Cold Beam OTHER. Corrected to match the source.

priority.node: Level nodes for shard efficiency rather than pushing each skill to 25 before starting the next.
priority.why: The class doc, verbatim: 'I don't recommend sending every skill immediately to level 25 using your node shards before moving on to the next. Instead, to be node efficient, you may choose to spend some nodes on a slightly lower priority skill, as it will level up more quickly.'

priority.node: Park Mana Overload at level 1, 10 or 20 before eventually pushing to 30.
priority.why: The class doc, verbatim: 'Mana Overload increases your final damage by 1% at every 10th level, so you may opt to let it sit at level 1/10/20 for a while before sending it to level 30. The levels outside of these breakpoints don't really do anything.'
priority.consensusNote: Single source (class doc), but stated as a flat mechanical fact rather than an opinion, and quoted verbatim.

priority.node: Craft Decent Holy Symbol as early as possible; later max Erda Fountain, Decent Holy Symbol, and Rope Lift / Blink.
priority.why: The class doc, verbatim: 'You also want to craft Decent Holy Symbol ASAP for training exp and drop rate' and 'you will also want to eventually max out rope lift/blink for the free stat/matt. For training purposes, maxing Erda Fountain will make it more likely to 1- or 2-shot mobs, and maxing Decent Holy Symbol will provide a bit of extra exp and drop rate.'

priority.node: CONTESTED - V skill (5th job) leveling order, KMS-side claim only: Bolt Barrage > Jupiter Thunder > Spirit of Snow = Frost Ark.
priority.why: NamuWiki's 5th job 'job core' section states verbatim: 'The reinforcement order is Thunder Break > Jupiter Thunder > Spirit of Snow = Frost Arc.' Thunder Break is the machine translation of Bolt Barrage and Frost Arc of Frost Ark. The GMS Heroic class doc has its own V-skill priority chart but publishes it only as an image, which could not be transcribed, so this ordering is NOT confirmed for GMS Heroic.
priority.consensusNote: Single source, KMS balance, machine-translated. The attribution is exact - NamuWiki does say this - but the claim is not corroborated for GMS Heroic and is flagged contested.

trios.trio: Chain Lightning / Thunder Sphere / Lightning Orb
trios.label: Primary trio (mystyjl: 'Trio #1'; Grandis Library: 'Primary Trio')
trios.why: Two sources give the same three-skill packing and both put it first. mystyjl's cross-class trio reference lists it as Trio #1; Grandis Library's recommended-nodes data labels the identical set 'Primary Trio'. Grandis adds: 'Any combination of these skills are good but preferred from same category as you want to max primary first'.
trios.consensusNote: Two sources that agree exactly, but only mystyjl is independent - Grandis credits its Boost Nodes Build to the class doc, so it belongs to the class doc family. Counted as 2 independent origins (mystyjl; class doc family), which is short of the 3 needed for strong.

trios.label: Secondary trio (mystyjl: 'Trio #2'; Grandis Library: 'Secondary Trio')
trios.why: The second trio, identical in both sources and second in both. Grandis notes '4 Boost Nodes total are needed to reach Master Level 60 for these skills (with Matrix Points used)' and that 'Nodes with the same Main Skill (skill at the top) cannot be equipped at the same time'.
trios.consensusNote: Same two sources, same independence caveat as the primary trio.

vMatrix.triosOrderingNote: The rank field is safe to read as priority: Grandis explicitly labels the two trios Primary and Secondary and says to max primary first, and mystyjl numbers them #1 and #2. This is a stated ranking, not an artifact of array order.
vMatrix.notes: Two different things are described here and should not be confused. The class doc, Grandis Library and NamuWiki describe boost node GROUPS, i.e. which skills a single node type boosts: Chain Lightning alone; Frozen Orb with Blizzard; Lightning Orb alone; Thunder Sphere with Elquines; Frost Ward with Ice Strike; Thunder Bolt with Cold Beam. mystyjl and Grandis's 'recommended nodes' block instead describe TRIO packing, i.e. which three skills to keep together on one trio node. The two views agree on which six skills matter. RESOLVED 2026-09-12: an earlier pass recorded that Grandis's Primary/Secondary/Other tier labels extracted inconsistently across two reads and therefore refused to record them. The instability was a rendered-text extraction artifact. The page's own embedded page data carries the tiers unambiguously (primary = node groups 1-4, secondary = group 5, other = group 6) and they are now recorded above. The trio packing was also upgraded from single-source: mystyjl (dated 2024-11-21, underlying test data 2024-05-14) is now corroborated by Grandis's identical Primary/Secondary trios. The class doc's changelog still records a V-matrix change on 2026-06-19, which postdates mystyjl, so mystyjl alone would be stale; Grandis (GMS v269 stamp) carries the corroboration.

order.step: Unlock the four mastery cores before unlocking Sol Janus.
order.why: The class doc, verbatim: 'I highly recommend unlocking Sol Janus after unlocking masteries.' The four mastery cores are named in the doc's own VI Job Skills section as Hexa Chain Lightning, Hexa Frozen Orb / Blizzard, Hexa Lightning Orb / Cryoshock, and Hexa Thunder Sphere / Hexa Elquines. maplestorywiki confirms the same core names, and NamuWiki lists the same four (Chain Lightning VI; Frozen Orb VI / Blizzard VI; Lightning Spear VI; Thunder Spear VI / Elquines VI).
order.consensusNote: The ordering advice - masteries before Sol Janus - is single-source (class doc). The identity and contents of the four mastery cores are confirmed by three independent sources. Labelled moderate because the actionable part of the claim is the ordering.

order.step: Optional swap: unlock HEXA Frozen Orb before HEXA Chain Lightning if training matters more to you than bossing.
order.why: The class doc, verbatim: 'You may opt to unlock Hexa Frozen Orb before Hexa Chain Lightning as it makes training much easier.' The doc's skill entry explains why: the HEXA core 'Increases the damage of the skills, and makes Frozen Orb much larger. Frozen Orb also will no longer stop at the end of platforms, or slow down for normal monsters, making it a much better mobbing skill.'
order.consensusNote: Single source (class doc), but stated as an explicit player-choice branch rather than a fixed order, and quoted verbatim.

order.step: Max HEXA Stat I after Jupiter Thunder Boost is unlocked. Max HEXA Stat II after Thunder Sphere reaches level 9.
order.why: The class doc, verbatim: 'The Hexa Stat upgrade in the list shows that after unlocking Jupiter Thunder Boost, Hexa Stat I should be upgraded to maximum. After Thunder Sphere is level 9, you can then upgrade Hexa Stat II to maximum and so on.' These are the two explicit HEXA Stat entry points the doc gives in prose, describing where the Stat upgrades sit inside its own image-only priority chart.
order.consensusNote: Single source (class doc), text-confirmed rather than inferred from an image.

order.step: Take Sol Janus after the masteries. If you train more than roughly 30 minutes a day, push it to level 10 or 20 early; level 30 only if you grind heavily.
order.why: The class doc, verbatim: 'If you train more than ~30 minutes a day, I'd also recommend considering getting Sol Janus to level 10 or even 20 early on, as it grants a very good amount of bonus experience at those level thresholds. You can even send it to level 30 if you're a giga grinder!' The doc's skill entry describes the two modes: 'Dusk activates meteors that hit enemies in a very large area around you with a three second cooldown. Dawn provides another set of summons (1 at level 1, up to 2 at level 10, up to 3 at level 20+) that last up to 2m at max rank.'
order.correctionNote: An earlier version compressed Dawn's scaling to 'from one at level 1 to three at level 20+', dropping the level 10 step. Corrected to the doc's exact figures.

order.step: CONTESTED - HEXA enhancement (boost) core order, KMS-side claim: Bolt Barrage Boost > Jupiter Thunder Boost > Spirit of Snow Boost = Frost Ark Boost.
order.why: NamuWiki's 6th job 'reinforced core' section states verbatim: 'Both skills have no options other than the final damage. That's why the reinforcement priority and order are the same as the fifth in the order of Thunder Brake > Jupiter Thunder > Spirit of Snow = Frost Arc.' This is a KMS-balance claim. The GMS Heroic class doc's own chart could not be read, and its prose places Jupiter Thunder Boost early enough to gate HEXA Stat I, which does not obviously match putting Bolt Barrage Boost first. Do not treat this as settled for GMS Heroic.
order.consensusNote: Single source, KMS balance, machine-translated, and in unresolved tension with the GMS doc's prose. The attribution is exact - NamuWiki does say this, with that reasoning.

hexa.notes: IMPORTANT GAP, recorded rather than filled. The authoritative GMS Heroic HEXA investment order for this class exists and is credited inside the class doc to a community member named Ebola, but it is published only as an infographic image, captioned 'Made for Reboot by Ebola'. The image was retrieved and inspected in an earlier pass: it is a long sequence of skill icons each annotated with a target level, and the icons are not individually identifiable at the published resolution, so the step-by-step order is NOT reproduced here. Guessing it would have been fabrication. Grandis Library's page data independently corroborates the credit, listing a '6th Job' infographic credited to Ebola dated 2026-06-25, but does not republish a readable copy (the image path in that data does not resolve). What the class doc says about the chart in prose IS recorded and was re-verified verbatim on 2026-09-12: 'This order is based on what upgrades give you the most Final Damage per Sol Erda Fragment in a full rotation'; the author 'has opted to instead focus on major breakpoints to park each skill before then focusing on something else'; and 'This graphic also prioritizes full rotation: if you'd rather focus on improving your burst, you may want to more heavily prioritize getting Origin levels and Jupiter Thunder levels.' Node structure is fully name-validated against the class doc's own VI Job Skills section and maplestorywiki: the origin skill is Frozen Lightning and the ascent skill is Parabolic Bolt; the four enhancement cores are Frost Ark Boost, Bolt Barrage Boost, Spirit of Snow Boost and Jupiter Thunder Boost; the common cores are Sol Janus (Dusk/Dawn) and Sol Hecate (Styx/Charon/Phlegethon). NamuWiki additionally lists a third skill core not yet live in GMS, matching the class doc's own 'Future Changes' entry for the KMS MapleStory Overdrive update, and the doc notes 'Two more Common Nodes will eventually be released later on.'

hyperStats.orderingNote: This is an UNORDERED set, not a ranking. It contains one entry because that is the only hyper stat allocation any source states for this class. The class doc explicitly refuses to publish a fixed hyper stat order and defers to per-character optimisation. Downstream code must not read array position here as priority.

priority.stat: Critical Rate to level 7 (9% crit rate)
priority.why: The class doc, verbatim: 'I recommend getting 3% crit rate from Familiar Badges, and then 9% crit rate from Level 7 Hyper Stat to put you at exactly 100% crit combined with the above sources.' The doc immediately adds that hyper stat and Legion are interchangeable contributors: 'You can also put legion blocks into critical rate and reduce the amount of Hyper Stat Points allocated to critical rate. Note that you can optimize your hyper stat vs. legion contribution to crit rate using Maple Scouter.'

hyperStats.notes: No full hyper stat allocation order is recorded, because none could be sourced. The class doc publishes its hyper stat and critical rate figures as images and its prose gives only the critical rate target. The doc explicitly says the hyper stat versus Legion split for critical rate should be optimised per character with Maple Scouter rather than read off a fixed list. That deferral is itself the finding: a static hyper stat priority list for this class is not what the maintainers recommend. A useful class-specific detail that IS text-confirmed: the doc says 'With the recent changes to our class transforming infinity into a passive skill, we can now afford crit rate blocks into our legion grid', which changes how much hyper stat needs to go into critical rate compared to older guides. If critical rate is short on a less progressed account, the doc suggests the Phantom link skill as a temporary substitute until other sources come online.

hyperSkills.orderingNote: An UNORDERED set of five picks, not a ranking. The class doc groups them rather than ranking them: Chain Lightning - Reinforce, Chain Lightning - Extra Strike and Frozen Orb - Reinforce are the damage lines it says should always be taken; Teleport Mastery - Range is the utility pick; Chain Lightning - Spread is the flexible fifth. Downstream code must not read array position as priority.

passives.why: The class doc, verbatim: 'Teleport Mastery: Range is great for movement and gives I/L one of the longest teleports in the game. It is not a passive, but a toggle that you can drag from the skill tab to your keyboard layout. Note that it does not stack with Teleport Boost: you can only have one of Teleport Mastery: Range or Teleport Boost activated at once.'
passives.consensusNote: Class doc and Grandis Library list the same five picks, but Grandis's own credits block assigns its Hyper Passive Build to the class doc, so this is one source family, not two opinions.

passives.why: The class doc, verbatim: 'Chain Lightning: Reinforce, +1 Hit, and Frozen Orb: Reinforce are the best options for increasing I/L's damage, and so should always be taken.'
passives.consensusNote: Class doc, restated by Grandis Library, which credits its Hyper Passive Build to the class doc - one source family.

passives.why: This is the line the class doc calls '+1 Hit' in the sentence grouping it with Chain Lightning Reinforce and Frozen Orb Reinforce as the best damage options, always taken. Grandis Library lists it under its GMS name, Chain Lightning - Extra Strike.
passives.consensusNote: Class doc, restated by Grandis Library (not independent). The name mapping from the doc's '+1 Hit' to the GMS skill name is supplied by Grandis and by maplestorywiki.

passives.why: Third of the three damage lines the class doc names in the 'should always be taken' sentence.
passives.consensusNote: Class doc, restated by Grandis Library (not independent).

passives.why: The class doc, verbatim: 'Chain Lightning: Spread is simply the best remaining fifth option, but really isn't needed for I/L to have sufficient mobbing. The only real alternative is Frozen Orb: Spread, which can help mobbing slightly once Hexa Frozen Orb is unlocked.'
passives.consensusNote: Class doc, restated by Grandis Library (not independent); the doc itself presents this slot as flexible.

hyperSkills.notes: Five passive picks total. The fifth slot is the only genuine decision: Chain Lightning - Spread by default, Frozen Orb - Spread if you value mobbing and have HEXA Frozen Orb unlocked. No sourced recommendation on the active hyper skills was found - the class doc's HYPER SKILL PASSIVES section covers passives only and says nothing about the active hyper skills - so that field is left empty rather than guessed. Note on sourceCount: every entry here is 1, not 2, because Grandis Library's credits block assigns its Hyper Passive Build to the class doc. Grandis is listed in sources as the corroborating transcription of an image-only list, not as a second opinion.

bossing.orderingNote: Listed in the order Grandis Library lists them, which corresponds to inner ability line slots 1, 2 and 3. That ordering is a slot assignment, not a rolling order - see rollingStrategy, where the class doc tells you to roll the Boss Damage line FIRST because it is the hardest to hit.
lines: Damage to monsters inflicted with Abnormal Status +8%
bossing.why: The class doc's ideal bossing inner ability is published as an image, but its surrounding prose names each line: it tells you to 'roll first for 10% Boss Damage, which is the harder line to get', and then to 'wait for a discount honor event, lock the boss damage, and roll for Attack Speed +1 and Abnormal Status Damage.' Grandis Library's page data lists the same three lines verbatim as 'Attack Speed +1', 'Boss Damage +10%', 'Damage to monsters inflicted with Abnormal Status +8%', supplying the +8% figure the doc's prose does not give.
bossing.consensusNote: One source family (class doc, restated by Grandis Library, which credits its Inner Ability section to the class doc). The three lines are text-confirmed in the doc's prose, not read off an image; the +8% abnormal-status figure comes from Grandis only.
bossing.correctionNote: An earlier version listed Boss Damage +10% first and Attack Speed +1 second, and paraphrased the third line as 'Damage to abnormal status afflicted monsters' with no value. Reordered to the source's own listing order and the third line restored to its full name and value.

earlyGame.orderingNote: These are ALTERNATIVES, not a set to assemble. The doc offers either one as an acceptable early result.
earlyGame.why: The class doc, verbatim: 'While it may be tempting to try and go for this inner ability as a new player, it is very expensive, and as such it is recommended you settle for good-but-not-perfect options while saving money for gear upgrades and honor for an inner ability discount event. You can consider Attack Speed +1 or Boss Damage +20% as a good early game Inner Ability.'

training.orderingNote: Slot order, from Grandis Library. The first two lines are the same ability at different value caps - Grandis's own note reads 'Depending on what's chosen as the 1st Line, choose the other for the 2nd Line', i.e. the +20% first line and the +15% second line are the meso and drop halves of the same pair in whichever arrangement you roll.
training.why: The class doc says a dedicated grinding preset became standard once multiple inner ability presets arrived ('As of the GO WEST/Dreamer update, there are multiple Inner Ability presets, and so you can have a dedicated preset for grinding'), but publishes its own grinding preset as an image that could not be read. These specific lines and values are quoted verbatim from Grandis Library's page data, which credits its Inner Ability section to the class doc.
training.consensusNote: One source family, and the underlying doc's own version of this preset was not readable, so Grandis is the only actual text for the line values.
training.correctionNote: An earlier version recorded 'Meso Obtained +20%', 'Drop Rate +20%', 'Damage to normal monsters +8%'. Two errors: the first two lines are the combined 'Meso Obtained / Item Drop Rate' ability, not separate meso and drop abilities, and the second line caps at +15%, not +20%. As previously recorded the file described an inner ability that cannot be rolled. Corrected to Grandis's exact strings.

rollingStrategy.why: Roll first for Boss Damage +10%, which the class doc calls 'the harder line to get', using Miracle Circulators on a second preset 'to maintain your original IA'. The doc gives two reasons for circulators verbatim: 'first because it's the only way to reset your inner ability without using honor (a very hard to come by resource in Heroic servers), and second because Miracle Circulators always provide the highest value for a given inner ability line (Unique Boss Damage ranges from 5%-10%)'. They are purchasable for meso in the GMS Heroic Cash Shop. On cost: 'the average cost for this roll is around 5B, and can easily cost upwards of 10-20B if you get unlucky'. Then 'ideally wait for a discount honor event, lock the boss damage, and roll for Attack Speed +1 and Abnormal Status Damage.' A separate party-bossing preset is worth keeping if you regularly party with attack speed buffers such as Buccaneer.
rollingStrategy.consensusNote: Single source (class doc), text-confirmed verbatim throughout.

innerAbility.notes: The doc's ideal-bossing and grinding presets are both published as images; the three bossing lines above are recovered from the doc's surrounding prose, which names each of them, and from Grandis Library's text, which supplies the exact values. The party-bossing preset's exact contents are image-only and are not recorded.

gearingNotes: STAFF, NOT WAND - this is the class-specific gearing call most likely to be got wrong. A wand offers extra critical rate, but the class doc says the staff's higher base magic attack outweighs it. The common counter-argument that a staff's slower weapon attack speed is a drawback is wrong for a mage: mages use casting speed, not weapon attack speed, and casting speed has a base attack speed level of 4 regardless of which weapon is held. ATTACK SPEED - the GMS cap is 10 and I/L reaches it from the sources the doc lists; the soft cap of 8 cannot be broken without a Green Potion, so a Green Potion is part of the endgame buff set rather than optional. CRITICAL RATE - the target is 100%. The doc's route is the baseline account sources it lists plus 3% from Familiar Badges plus 9% from level 7 Critical Rate hyper stat. Because Infinity was reworked into a passive skill, Legion critical rate blocks became affordable for this class, so critical rate can be shifted between hyper stat and Legion; the doc recommends optimising that split with Maple Scouter rather than fixing it. Phantom link skill is a stopgap for less progressed accounts. SECONDARY - Deimos Sage Shield, crafted from a recipe dropped by Cygnus. It is preferred over magic book secondaries because it can be starforced to 20 stars, giving more magic attack and stat. It later converts to the Astra Arcane Shield; a shield above 15 stars can only transfer into a Stage 2 or higher Astra Arcane Shield, and a fully starforced transfer costs around 10 billion meso. On Interactive servers the shield is cheap on the Auction House. WSE - the target is 9 lines of attack across weapon, secondary and emblem, but the doc says to check Maple Scouter for whether boss damage lines beat attack lines on your specific setup, and not to worry about temporarily settling for a boss line on the Genesis weapon or the shield. COOLDOWN HAT - a -2s line is the standard because it smooths the burst rotation. I/L does not directly profit from cooldown reduction the way some classes do, so casual players clearing around the 15 minute mark can stay on a stat hat. Late and endgame players may want -4s on Heroic or -5s on Interactive for tight-timer fights such as Baldrix, Limbo and Seren. Note the doc's own update on this: once the KMS change reducing the maximum boss timer to 20 minutes lands, the threshold for squeezing in an extra burst becomes -6s, so the doc's recommendation is to stay at -2s rather than buy an intermediate cooldown hat, unless you specifically want a dedicated culvert hat. FREEZE STACKS - the resource the whole kit is built on. Ice skills apply stacks, lightning skills consume them, and Frozen Orb used off cooldown is the primary source. The payouts are: +20 final damage from Storm Magic at one or more stacks; +10% critical damage from Frost Clutch at five stacks, rising to 16% with Glacial Fury at 2% per stack; +1% final damage on lightning skills per stack consumed; and +10% ignore DEF from Shatter, rising to 16% with Glacial Fury at 2% per stack. Glacial Fury also raises the stack cap from 5 to 8, which is what scales all of the above. Notably Jupiter Thunder is net positive on stacks - it consumes 6 over its full duration but returns about 21 on average, because a stack is only consumed every third proc while Blizzard can final-attack on every proc.

commonMistakes.mistake: Picking a wand over a staff for the extra critical rate.
commonMistakes.why: The staff's higher base magic attack is worth more than the wand's critical rate.

commonMistakes.mistake: Avoiding a staff because its weapon attack speed is slow.
commonMistakes.why: Mages use casting speed, not the weapon's base attack speed, so the weapon's attack speed rating is irrelevant. The doc calls this out specifically as a common misconception.

commonMistakes.mistake: Sending every V skill node straight to level 25 in strict priority order.
commonMistakes.why: Shards go further if spent on a slightly lower-priority skill that will gain levels faster.

commonMistakes.mistake: Levelling Mana Overload through its non-breakpoint levels.
commonMistakes.why: It only pays out at every tenth level, so levels 2 through 9, 11 through 19 and 21 through 29 do nothing.

commonMistakes.mistake: Chasing the perfect bossing inner ability as a new player.
commonMistakes.why: The doc is explicit that it is very expensive and that meso and honor are better saved for gear upgrades and a discount event; a single good line is the correct early target.
With the 20 minute boss timer change, the threshold for gaining an extra burst moves to -6s, so cooldown between -2s and -6s buys nothing. Stay at -2s.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forcing the mini-burst when it would desync the 2 minute cycle.
commonMistakes.why: The doc says I/L's mini-burst is not very impactful and recommends skipping it rather than delaying, both to keep the 2 minute burst on schedule and to avoid dragging out a party run.

commonMistakes.mistake: Letting freeze stacks lapse and overthinking how to maintain them.
commonMistakes.why: The doc's position is that there is no technique to it - Frozen Orb used off cooldown is the primary source and is sufficient.

sources.what: The Arch Mage (Ice, Lightning) class doc, maintained by PommeCuite (Discord zatchounet) for the Explorer Mage Discord, inherited from Vivillon. Scoped explicitly to GMS Heroic and Interactive. The authoritative judgement source for this class: boost nodes, V-skill priority, HEXA matrix priority (chart credited to Ebola and captioned 'Made for Reboot'), HEXA stat, hyper skill passives, attack speed, critical rate, inner ability, legion grid, link skills, freeze stack mechanics, burst order and rotations, culvert, and a boss/champion mule assessment. MAJOR LIMITATION: every ordered priority list in this doc is published as an embedded image, not text. Retrieve as plain text with /export?format=txt; the /mobilebasic and normal document URLs return less. The HEXA priority image was extracted and inspected but its icon steps are not individually identifiable, so the ordering is not transcribed anywhere in this file.
sources.dated: 2026-07-25 (latest changelog entry; header reads 2026-06-18, GMS Ride The Lightning / KMS Crown)

sources.what: Grandis Library class page. Supplies the six boost node groups with their contents AND their Primary/Secondary/Other tiers, two recommended boost node trios labelled Primary and Secondary, the full example skill build path for jobs 1 to 4, the five hyper skill passive picks, recommended inner ability split into bossing and training with exact values, and base stats from skills. Has NO 6th job or HEXA investment section, though its metadata does credit a '6th Job' infographic to Ebola dated 2026-06-25. READING NOTE: the rendered page text extracts the tier labels unreliably - two earlier reads disagreed, and a third disagreed again. The page's embedded structured data is unambiguous and is what this file now relies on: primary = node groups 1-4, secondary = group 5, other = group 6.
sources.dated: GMS Ver. 269 [Ride the Lightning Update] sitewide stamp - two patches behind the v.271 target
sources.dependencyEvidence: The page's own Credits block reads: Skill Icons + Animations: Ikasuu | Inner Ability + Hyper Passive Build + Boost Nodes Build: Class Doc. Those are precisely the three judgement fields taken from it, so it is a restatement of the class doc and must not be counted as a second opinion.

sources.what: NamuWiki KMS skill page for Arch Mage (Ice, Lightning), read machine-translated to English. Genuinely independent of the Western guide-writing community. Independently confirms the six boost node groups and their contents, names the same four as an 'Essential Reinforcing Core' set headed by the matching 6th job core names, marks Glacial Wall / Ice Strike as the 'select strengthening core' and leaves Cold Beam / Thunderbolt out of both tiers, notes Ice Strike's narrow use in training builds before HEXA Frozen Orb, and is the only source found that states an explicit V-skill and HEXA enhancement core order. Also lists a third HEXA skill core not yet live in GMS. contest.method: An independent agent re-searched every claim in this file without seeing the researcher's reasoning, and was instructed to refute rather than confirm.
contest.resolutionMethod: Endgame-only resolution pass. Every claim in vMatrix, hexa, hyperSkills, hyperStats and innerAbility was re-opened at its own cited page - class doc via /export?format=txt, Grandis Library including its embedded page data, NamuWiki through a browser session (it 403s plain fetches), mystyjl NodeGuide - and each was confirmed verbatim, corrected to match the source, or deleted. No new sources were introduced.

resolved.defect: innerAbility.training records 'Drop Rate +20%' as the second line, sourced solely to Grandis Library. Grandis actually says 'Meso Obtained/Item Drop Rate +20%, Meso Obtained/Item Drop Rate +15%, Damage to Normal Monsters +8%'. The second line is +15%, not +20%, reflecting the real second/third-slot value cap. As recorded, the file describes an inner ability that cannot be rolled.
resolved.what: Re-read Grandis Library's page data. The defect is upheld and was in fact understated: the file had split one combined ability into two, as well as getting the second value wrong. The lines are now recorded exactly as the source gives them - 'Meso Obtained / Item Drop Rate +20%', 'Meso Obtained / Item Drop Rate +15%', 'Damage to Normal Monsters +8%' - together with Grandis's own note that the first and second lines are the two halves of the same pair. An ordered:true flag now says the array is slot order, sourced.

resolved.defect: 'so boost node investment is also the gate on 6th job progress' (vMatrix.priority[0].why) states a gating mechanic no source asserts. The class doc presents boost nodes and mastery cores as separate upgrade tracks and never says one gates the other. The group-to-core alignment is real and wiki-confirmed; the causal gate is invented connective tissue.
resolved.what: The gating clause is deleted - re-reading the class doc's BOOST NODES and VI JOB SKILLS sections confirms it says only 'Ice/Lightning has four relevant boost nodes that must be upgraded first' and describes the two tracks separately. The underlying correspondence is real and is now stated in each source's own words instead: Grandis Library defines its PRIMARY tier as 'Boost Nodes that unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery and are skills that are frequently used', NamuWiki heads its Essential Reinforcing Core table with the matching VI core names, and the class doc describes each of the five skills as 'Boosted by V Boost nodes' and 'given a VI Job Mastery Core'. The word 'unlock' now appears only as a quotation attributed to Grandis, never as a progression gate asserted by this file.

resolved.defect: FOUND DURING THIS PASS, not in the original defect list: vMatrix.priority[1] claimed 'Grandis Library ranks both in its lowest tier' about Frost Ward + Ice Strike and Thunder Bolt + Cold Beam.
resolved.what: A citation inversion of the same kind the pass was looking for. Grandis's page data puts Frost Ward + Ice Strike in SECONDARY ('don't unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery but are still used') and only Thunder Bolt + Cold Beam in OTHER ('do not need to be upgraded or has least priority'). NamuWiki agrees with the split, calling Glacial Wall / Ice Strike a 'select strengthening core' and omitting Cold Beam / Thunderbolt entirely. The entry now records two tiers rather than one and is upgraded to two-source moderate consensus.

resolved.defect: FOUND DURING THIS PASS: the file's conflicts block said Grandis's tier labels were unrecordable because rendered-text extraction disagreed across reads, yet vMatrix.priority[0] recorded a tier claim anyway ('Grandis Library tiers these same four above the remaining two'). An internal contradiction.
resolved.what: The tier claim turned out to be true and is now properly sourced. The instability was a rendering artifact; the page's embedded data gives primary = groups 1-4, secondary = group 5, other = group 6. Tier labels are now recorded with that provenance stated, and the conflicts entry is marked resolved instead of left open.

resolved.what: The class doc says '1 at level 1, up to 2 at level 10, up to 3 at level 20+' and that they 'last up to 2m at max rank'. Restored to the doc's exact figures.

endgameVerification.statement: Every claim in the five endgame sections was re-opened at its own cited page in this pass and is now either quoted from that page or explicitly labelled as the gap it is. Two claims were corrected for value errors, three for mis-stated attributions, two array shapes were flagged as unordered, and two claims were upgraded after finding genuine corroboration.
